## Learning objectives

Define a counted-allele dosage; fit a restricted eQTL-style mean model with covariates; compare correlated candidate evidence; distinguish association, prediction and mediation.

## Biological question and data

Does marker1 associate with the fictional gene01 expression profile after accounting for diet and batch?

The generator supplies a marker1 effect on gene01 log expected expression, as well as diet and batch effects. Animals are unrelated/independent in the model. The supplied exposure is known. The quasi-Poisson working model is not a calibrated GWAS/eQTL pipeline for real related animals.

No biological download is required. Numerical inputs are hypothetical, not observed animal data. The runnable examples use base R. Count and abundance units are specified where used.

## 1. Align the counted allele and expression

The 0/1/2 dosage counts a fictional designated allele. Keep sample IDs and the exposure offset explicit.

```{r}
helper_dir <- if (dir.exists("R")) "R" else "../R"
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(helper_dir,"teaching_data.R")))
source(file.path(helper_dir,"teaching_data.R"))
d <- teaching_data()
meta <- d$metadata
meta$dosage <- d$genotypes[meta$animal,"marker1"]
meta$count <- as.vector(d$counts["gene01",meta$animal])
meta$exposure <- unname(d$exposure[meta$animal])
stopifnot(all(meta$dosage%in%0:2),qr(model.matrix(~diet+batch+dosage,meta))$rank==4)
table(meta$dosage)
```

A dosage cannot be called favourable or causal from its numeric coding.

## 2. Fit the supplied expression-association model

Use diet, batch, dosage and exposure. Translate the dosage coefficient into expected expression ratio per counted allele.

```{r}
fit <- glm(count~diet+batch+dosage+offset(log(exposure)),data=meta,family=quasipoisson())
tab <- coef(summary(fit))
tab
c(log_effect_per_allele=coef(fit)["dosage"],
 mean_expression_ratio_per_allele=exp(coef(fit)["dosage"]),
 supplied_generator_ratio=exp(.3))
```

The fitted estimate need not equal exp(.3) in one count realization. The uncertainty belongs to a restricted working variance model, not a qualified biological eQTL analysis.

## 3. Create a correlated candidate and examine ambiguity

A nearly identical marker can tag the same signal. Genotype correlation is not an independent confirmation.

```{r}
candidate <- meta$dosage
candidate[1] <- (candidate[1]+1)%%3
c(dosage_correlation=cor(meta$dosage,candidate))
second <- glm(count~diet+batch+candidate+offset(log(exposure)),data=meta,family=quasipoisson())
c(marker1_effect=coef(fit)["dosage"],tagged_candidate_effect=coef(second)["candidate"])
stopifnot(length(candidate)==48)
```

A correlated candidate can inherit association. Two conditional models here do not calculate a fine-mapping posterior or identify a causal allele.

## Interpretation and limits

Real studies need allele/reference alignment, genotype and expression QC, relatedness/structure treatment, adequate replication, cis/trans definitions, multiple testing and model diagnostics. A TWAS association is not automatically evidence that expression mediates the variant–trait effect. Fine-mapping requires an explicit candidate/model/LD framework.

## Exercises

1. What is the expected ratio per allele in the generator?
2. Does a correlated candidate represent another independent biological effect?
3. What would an expression-mediation claim additionally require?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Suggested answers"}
1. exp(.3), about 1.35, conditional on the supplied model.
2. No; association can be tagged through correlated dosage.
3. Temporal/causal assumptions and evidence addressing shared genetic and environmental drivers, not merely paired association tests.
:::
